meta.subject: Chinese character strip skipped after the LIS-10723 data-source upgrade
meta.author: LIS Team

slides.headline:
Chinese characters reach Sybase
when the Oracle flag is not read
slides.lede: lis-patient-pmi-sync-svc strips Chinese characters when the hospital is on Sybase. After the LIS-10723 data-source upgrade, that flag check does not reach Oracle, so the strip is skipped.
slides.notes: Patient sync is supposed to strip Chinese characters when the hospital is on Sybase. After the LIS-10723 data-source upgrade, the flag check does not reach Oracle, so the strip never runs.

slides.title: Six stops

items.title: Existing Design
items.note: the flag check does not reach Oracle

items.title: Proposed Change
items.note: read the flag, then strip when Sybase

items.title: Open Questions
items.note: one Oracle database, and an open transaction

slides.notes: Six stops. The story is the skipped strip, then the Oracle flag read that turns it back on.

slides.title: The strip is skipped, so Chinese characters land in Sybase

steps.title: Chinese characters are stripped for Sybase
steps.body: Before a message is stored, patient sync removes Chinese characters when the hospital database is Sybase.

steps.title: data-source gained transaction locking
steps.body: The library upgrade for transaction locking left the Oracle flag check unable to reach Oracle.

steps.title: The strip does not run
steps.body: Chinese characters are inserted into Sybase.

callout.text: The Oracle flag. When the check fails, the replace is skipped.

slides.notes: The flag is the only thing that turns the strip on. When the check fails, the program skips the replace and Sybase gets the Chinese characters.

slides.title: The flag check does not reach Oracle

left.label: Today
left.title: The strip is skipped
points: Check: Oracle flag is not read
Result: replace logic does not run
Store: Chinese characters go into Sybase

right.label: Proposed
right.title: Read the flag on Oracle
points: Check: connect to Oracle and read the flag

slides.notes: We do not move the hospital transaction onto Oracle. That would commit hospital work already done. Only the flag read uses the Oracle connection.

slides.title: Read the Oracle flag, then strip when the hospital is Sybase

cards.title: Read the flag on Oracle
cards.body: Connect to Oracle and read the flag while the hospital database is still in use.

cards.title: Sybase means replace
cards.body: If the flag says the hospital is Sybase, replace the Chinese characters.

cards.title: Hospital work stays open
cards.body: Do not switch the hospital transaction over to Oracle.

slides.notes: The replace logic is already in lis-patient-pmi-sync-svc. The library fix is what lets that check succeed.

slides.title: Ship the library and leave config alone

cards.title: New data-source build
cards.body: Services take the fix by depending on the new library build.

cards.title: No config change
cards.body: JDBC settings stay as they are in DEVQA, SIT, and PROD.

cards.title: Patient sync only rebuilds
cards.body: lis-patient-pmi-sync-svc rebuilds to take the library. Its own source stays the same.

slides.notes: DEVQA, SIT, and PROD keep the same JDBC settings. What changes is the library binary.

slides.title: Put the previous library back

cards.title: Redeploy and restart
cards.body: Put the previous data-source build back on the affected service and restart it.

cards.title: Watch for the old warning
cards.body: On a Sybase hospital, the log should again say defaulting to PostgreSQL.

cards.title: Clear a wrong saved answer
cards.body: Drop one cached type check for that hospital and lab.

slides.notes: You know the rollback worked when the old warning is back: defaulting to PostgreSQL. A wrong saved answer is cleared with DELETE /api/clearCachedDBConn/{hospital}/{lab}.

slides.title: Two questions before we build

asks.q: Is LOE / lab 1 / LOE_DB the only Oracle database?
asks.why: The flag read will use that connection unless the thread is already on Oracle.

asks.q: If a distributed transaction is already open, may this Oracle read join it?
asks.why: Hospital work will not be committed early. Transaction locking otherwise stays as LIS-10723 left it.

slides.notes: The first question is whether a second Oracle database is registered. The second is enlistment only. We are not redesigning transaction locking.

slides.headline: Q&A
slides.body: Patient sync source does not change. The strip runs again once the Oracle flag can be read.
slides.notes: Likely question: does patient sync source change? No. The strip is already there. It runs again once the Oracle flag can be read.

slides.headline: Read the flag, then strip for Sybase
slides.note: No schema change. No config change.
